stories.title: 🤗 Trending: meta-llama/Meta-Llama-3-8B
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: The news highlights the trending status of the Meta-Llama-3-8B model on Hugging Face.
It is categorized under key NLP/ML tags including 'transformers' and 'text-generation'.
The mention of Llama-3 indicates relevance to the latest advancements in large language models (LLMs).

stories.title: Muse Glimmer from Meta Superintelligence Labs is now available
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Meta has released Muse Glimmer, its first open model from Superintelligence Labs.
Muse Glimmer is a 30B multimodal model licensed under Apache 2.0, targeting local coding agents.
The model is optimized for local deployment via Ollama, featuring native DFlash and image input support.

stories.title: 🤗 Trending: deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-R1
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: The news highlights a trending model, deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-R1, on Hugging Face Benchmarks.
The model is categorized for text generation and conversational AI tasks.
It utilizes standard ML components like transformers and safetensors.

stories.title: 🤗 Trending: meta-llama/Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: The news highlights the trending status of the Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct model on Hugging Face.
It pertains to the text-generation pipeline, indicating its use in large language model applications.
The model is associated with key ML technologies like transformers and safetensors.

stories.title: NVIDIA Nemotron 3.5 Lightning
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: NVIDIA Nemotron 3.5 Lightning, a 30B parameter open model, is now accessible via Ollama.
The model is specifically designed for autonomous AI agents capable of multi-step tasks.
It is optimized to run locally on user hardware, supporting context gathering and tool calling.

stories.title: Ollama: all aboard open models
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama, a platform for running open models, has secured significant funding.
The company raised $88 million from prominent investors including Y Combinator and Benchmark.
Ollama currently serves a large developer base of 8.9 million users.

stories.title: Faster Gemma 4 on MLX with multi-token prediction
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Gemma 4 inference speed is significantly improved within Ollama 0.31 on Apple Silicon.
The performance boost is achieved through the implementation of Multi-Token Prediction (MTP) powered by MLX.
Coding agent performance using Gemma 4 saw up to a 90% speed increase on the Aider polyglot benchmark.

stories.title: Ollama's highest performance on Apple Silicon yet with MLX
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama has achieved its peak performance on Apple Silicon.
The performance boost is attributed to updates in the MLX engine.
Improvements include faster response times, higher output quality, and reduced memory usage.

stories.title: NVIDIA Nemotron 3 Ultra
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: NVIDIA is introducing Nemotron 3 Ultra, a new model architecture.
The model is specifically designed for high-throughput reasoning tasks.
It is optimized for supporting long-running agent workflows.

stories.title: One Basis to Animate Them All: Gaussian Blendshape Distillation for Real-Time Avatars
stories.author: Ivan Laptev
bullet_points: Addresses the computational bottleneck in real-time animation of 3D Gaussian avatars, which typically requires costly neural inference.
Proposes GALA (Gaussian Animation via Linear Approximation), a distillation method that approximates complex animation using linear combinations of blendshapes.
Replaces per-frame heavy neural decoding with a much lighter, shallow coefficient predictor for faster performance.

stories.title: KaliBench: A Fine-Grained Benchmark for Cybersecurity Tool Use on Kali Linux with Runtime-Free Verifiable Rewards
stories.author: Muzammal Naseer
bullet_points: Introduces KaliBench, a new benchmark specifically designed to evaluate LLMs' ability to generate executable commands for real-world cybersecurity tools on Kali Linux.
Addresses a critical gap in current evaluations by moving beyond knowledge-based or high-level agentic tasks to focus on precise CLI command generation.
Features runtime-free verifiable rewards, suggesting a novel and rigorous method for assessing command accuracy in security workflows.

stories.title: Reconstruct, Practice, Go Real: Guided Self-Improvement for Embodied Agents
stories.author: Haozhi Qi
bullet_points: Introduces RPG, a framework for autonomous improvement of robot execution systems.
Allows robots to improve capabilities without requiring updates to the underlying model weights.
The system uses offline datasets to identify skills and generates simulation tasks for practice using execution feedback.

stories.title: VISTA: A Visual Harness for Reasoning in an Interactive World
stories.author: Kaiming He
bullet_points: Introduces VISTA, a visual harness designed to unlock the reasoning potential of multimodal AI models.
VISTA provides general-purpose multimodal models with long-horizon vision capabilities in interactive environments.
The system maintains a lossless visual memory, allowing the model to actively retrieve past environmental observations.

stories.title: One Basis to Animate Them All: Gaussian Blendshape Distillation for Real-Time Avatars
stories.author: Ivan Laptev
bullet_points: Addresses the computational bottleneck in real-time animation of 3D Gaussian avatars, which typically relies on costly neural inference.
Proposes GALA (Gaussian Animation via Linear Approximation), a distillation method to approximate complex avatar animations using a linear combination of blendshapes.
Replaces per-frame heavy neural decoding with a much faster, shallow coefficient predictor for efficient animation.

stories.title: The Missing Primitive: Diagnosing and Repairing Mathematical Reasoning in Large Language Models
stories.author: Zhengzhong Tu
bullet_points: The research addresses the fundamental question of whether LLMs possess true structural mathematical understanding, despite impressive performance.
The paper introduces the concept of 'Mathematical Primitive' as a new diagnostic tool to probe LLM capabilities.
The findings aim to systematically diagnose mathematical weaknesses and guide future post-training improvements for LLMs.

stories.title: Ollama now supports Jev-style decision models
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama now integrates support for Jev-style decision models via TypeSafe's Jev API.
These models enable fast, low-latency, and cost-free execution for making decisions based on text input.
Decision models provide probabilistic answers to yes/no questions, choices, and scoring.

stories.title: Claude Desktop support with Ollama
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Claude Desktop now supports Ollama as a third-party gateway.
This integration allows users to run open-source models within the Claude Desktop environment.
It bridges proprietary AI platforms with local, open-source LLM ecosystems.

stories.title: Improved performance and model support with GGUF
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama 0.30 release introduces performance improvements and enhanced GGUF model compatibility.
The update leverages llama.cpp to broaden model support across various hardware configurations.
It strengthens Ollama's MLX engine specifically for Apple silicon users.

stories.title: Dots get up in Muse’s business
stories.author: Jacob Kastrenakes
bullet_points: OpenAI has released 'Dots,' a new product positioned as a business-first alternative to Muse.
Dots is a paid service, starting at a minimum cost of $100 per month.
The product appears to offer business-oriented features, contrasting with the more creative focus of Muse.

stories.title: Tesla will now let you drive off mid-charge if there’s an emergency
stories.author: Andrew J. Hawkins
bullet_points: Tesla has implemented a new feature allowing drivers to drive away from a Supercharger while charging.
This safety update was introduced following a mass shooting incident at a Supercharger location in Idaho.
Previously, driving was disabled while the vehicle was plugged into the charging port.

stories.title: Home Assistant says ‘Big tech ruined the cloud, so we’re out’
stories.author: Jennifer Pattison Tuohy
bullet_points: Home Assistant is rebranding its cloud service from 'Home Assistant Cloud' to 'Home Assistant Link'.
The move is driven by the platform's stance against the perceived negative impact of 'Big Tech' on cloud infrastructure.
This signals a continued push within the open-source community toward local, decentralized smart home control.

stories.title: TCL is right to question Samsung’s use of the term “Mini LED”
stories.author: Scharon Harding
bullet_points: The article challenges Samsung's definition of 'Mini LED' technology.
A key point of contention is whether a true Mini LED implementation requires Full Array Local Dimming (FALD).
This highlights industry debates over marketing terminology versus technical specifications in display technology.

stories.title: Hacks of 2 federal agencies in a month have spilled a bonanza of sensitive data
stories.author: Dan Goodin
bullet_points: Federal government cybersecurity has faced a significant downturn recently.
Two separate federal agencies experienced data breaches within the span of one month.
The breaches resulted in the exposure of a substantial amount of sensitive data.

stories.title: Judge dismisses Chegg and Penske antitrust lawsuits targeting Google AI search
stories.author: Ryan Whitwam
bullet_points: Judge dismissed antitrust lawsuits filed by Chegg and Penske against Google regarding its AI search.
The court ruled that the issues surrounding AI search are not classified as antitrust violations.
The ruling acknowledges that AI search technologies carry inherent consequences, but these do not constitute an antitrust problem.

stories.title: Memory executives expect RAM shortage to continue through 2028
stories.author: Scharon Harding
bullet_points: Memory executives anticipate that RAM shortages will persist through the year 2028.
Pricing trends indicate that memory costs for 2027 are projected to be significantly higher than those in 2026.
The report highlights sustained supply chain and demand pressures within the memory market.

stories.title: ScholarCatalyst: A Benchmark for Retrieving Papers That Inspire New Research
stories.author: Chelsea Finn
bullet_points: Introduces ScholarCatalyst, a new benchmark designed to evaluate AI's ability to find inspiring prior research papers.
The benchmark leverages expert human knowledge, where researchers annotate which past works influenced their current projects.
This addresses a key gap in AI research: the ability to synthesize and retrieve conceptually relevant, foundational ideas from vast literature archives.

stories.title: SILSA: Sliding-Window Slice Latents for Topology-Preserving High-Resolution 3D Generation
stories.author: Ismini Lourentzou
bullet_points: SILSA introduces a new framework for high-resolution 3D generation using compact sliding-window slice latents.
It addresses limitations in current methods (voxel latents/multi-stage pipelines) where surface fragmentation weakens topological consistency.
The approach aims to improve topological preservation and reduce generation costs compared to existing token-based methods.

stories.title: Hierarchical Continuous Diffusion Language Models
stories.author: Alexander Schwing
bullet_points: Introduces Continuous Diffusion Language Models as an alternative to discrete diffusion models for language generation.
Addresses a key limitation of discrete models: independent token sampling during parallel decoding, which breaks statistical dependencies.
Continuous diffusion models mitigate this by denoising a shared continuous state, though the current architecture limits the denoiser's view to only that state.

stories.title: DMAD: Distribution Matching as Adversarial Distillation for Fast Visual Generation
stories.author: Chongyang Ma
bullet_points: Introduces DMAD (Distribution Matching as Adversarial Distillation) for fast visual generation.
DMAD reframes distribution matching as a classification task to directly learn log-density ratios.
It aims to improve upon previous methods that required auxiliary diffusion models, reducing memory and computation overhead.

stories.title: Higher-Order Molecular Grammars for Generative and Foundation Models in Chemistry
stories.author: Tolga Birdal
bullet_points: Introduces Higher-order Grammar Representation (HGR) to improve molecular learning models.
Addresses the limitation of standard sequential/graph formalisms in encoding complex molecular topologies like ring systems.
Aims to provide a principled, topology-aware framework that is computationally feasible for generative and foundation models in chemistry.

stories.title: Embedding Prediction Helps Image Generation
stories.author: Stella X. Yu
bullet_points: The research proposes using predicted embeddings as a conditioning mechanism in diffusion transformers for image generation.
The core method, Next-Embedding Predictive Autoregression (NEPA), trains a Transformer to predict the next continuous embedding in a sequence.
This approach leverages the sequential nature of image generation (clean image following noisy image) to train the predictive model.

stories.title: SILSA: Sliding-Window Slice Latents for Topology-Preserving High-Resolution 3D Generation
stories.author: Ismini Lourentzou
bullet_points: SILSA introduces a new framework for high-resolution 3D generation using compact sliding-window slice latents.
It addresses limitations in existing methods (voxel latents/multi-stage pipelines) where surface fragmentation and topological inconsistency occur.
The core innovation is a topology-aware representation designed to improve consistency and reduce generation cost for complex shapes.

stories.title: TACO: Ternary Absolute-max Column-wise One-sparse Optimizer for LLM Fine-Tuning
stories.author: Aritra Dutta
bullet_points: TACO introduces a new optimizer designed to reduce the memory overhead associated with full-parameter fine-tuning of Large Language Models (LLMs).
The core innovation is a Ternary Absolute-max Column-wise One-sparse approach to optimize LLM training.
It addresses limitations of existing methods (like Muon) by offering a memory-efficient alternative while aiming to maintain performance comparable to AdamW.

stories.title: Cost-augmented Schrödinger bridges on graphs are exactly solvable: a Feynman-Kac tilt replaces learned control
stories.author: Akshay Balsubramani
bullet_points: Introduces an exact solution for cost-augmented Schrödinger bridges on graphs.
Replaces complex learned control methods (like temporal-difference penalties) with a Feynman-Kac tilt.
Simplifies the computation by transforming the problem into a standard bridge problem against a tilted reference process.

stories.title: Hierarchical Continuous Diffusion Language Models
stories.author: Alexander Schwing
bullet_points: Continuous Diffusion Language Models (CDLMs) are presented as an alternative to discrete diffusion models for language generation.
Discrete models suffer from a bottleneck where parallel decoding samples tokens independently, losing statistical dependencies.
CDLMs address this by denoising a shared continuous state, aiming to maintain inter-token dependencies during generation.

stories.title: Trust the Direction, Search the Step: Zero-and-First-Order Methods for LLM Fine-Tuning
stories.author: Aritra Dutta
bullet_points: Addresses the critical challenge of step-size selection in large-scale LLM fine-tuning optimization.
Introduces Zero-and-First-Order optimization (ZFO) to decouple direction selection from step-size.
ZFO uses a first-order optimizer for direction and zeroth-order evaluations along a 1D subspace for step-size determination.

stories.title: KaliBench: A Fine-Grained Benchmark for Cybersecurity Tool Use on Kali Linux with Runtime-Free Verifiable Rewards
stories.author: Muzammal Naseer
bullet_points: Introduces KaliBench, a new benchmark specifically designed to evaluate LLMs' ability to generate executable commands for real-world cybersecurity tools on Kali Linux.
Addresses a critical gap in current LLM evaluations, which often focus on knowledge or high-level tasks rather than precise CLI command generation.
Emphasizes the need for fine-grained evaluation due to the sensitivity of cybersecurity operations to minor syntax or flag errors.

stories.title: ScholarCatalyst: A Benchmark for Retrieving Papers That Inspire New Research
stories.author: Chelsea Finn
bullet_points: Introduces ScholarCatalyst, a new benchmark designed to test the ability to retrieve inspiring prior research papers.
Addresses the challenge of AI systems needing to identify relevant, often buried, prior ideas to advance new research.
Uses an automated pipeline based on researcher annotations to scale the creation of the benchmark dataset.

stories.title: Hierarchical Continuous Diffusion Language Models
stories.author: Alexander Schwing
bullet_points: Introduces Continuous Diffusion Language Models as an alternative to discrete diffusion models for language generation.
Addresses the structural bottleneck in discrete diffusion models where parallel decoding severs token statistical dependencies.
Continuous diffusion models mitigate this by denoising a shared continuous state, though the denoiser's view of this state is noted as limited.

stories.title: AutoCompact: Learning When to Compact Context in Long-Horizon Coding Agents
stories.author: Xin Dong
bullet_points: Introduces AutoCompact, a method to train coding agents to intelligently manage long-horizon context.
Addresses the challenge of context staleness in complex software engineering tasks (inspection, search, editing).
The agent learns when and how to compact its working state to maintain efficiency during long coding trajectories.

stories.title: Keyword Harnesses Fail Open: A Cheap Diagnostic Ladder for Tool-Use Claims in Small Language Models
stories.author: Juan S. Santillana
bullet_points: Keyword-matching benchmarks can generate false positives, incorrectly crediting small language models for tool use they do not actually perform.
The paper introduces a 'ladder of strict, cheap diagnostics' to accurately assess tool-use capabilities in smaller models.
The study demonstrates this issue using a matched-architecture pair of Spanish security language models, highlighting the limitations of lenient evaluation metrics.

stories.title: Finetuning with Sampling: SFT Learns Better Than You Think
stories.author: Yilun Du
bullet_points: The paper proposes a new finetuning method, 'Finetuning with Sampling,' to improve frontier models.
It challenges the conventional view that Reinforcement Learning (RL) is superior to Supervised Finetuning (SFT) for generalization.
The research explores the trade-offs between SFT's ability to use off-policy data and RL's generalization strengths.

stories.title: Argo-Bench: Evaluating Data Agents on Enterprise-Scale Workflows
stories.author: Joseph J Ma
bullet_points: Argo-Bench is a new evaluation framework designed to test Data Agents on complex, enterprise-scale workflows.
It addresses the limitations of existing text-to-SQL benchmarks, which only test query generation and often have flawed answer keys.
The framework uses public datasets to simulate real-world scenarios requiring reasoning across multiple tables and statistical analysis.

stories.title: Where-OPD: Spatially Guided On-Policy Self-Distillation of MLLMs with Synthetic Scenes
stories.author: Spyros Gidaris
bullet_points: The paper introduces 'Where-OPD,' a method applying on-policy self-distillation to Multimodal Large Language Models (MLLMs).
This technique aims to improve MLLM reasoning by using a privileged, self-generated version of the model for supervision.
It addresses a gap in current research, which primarily uses limited visual cues (like image crops) for fine-grained perception in MLLMs.

stories.title: Supabase is acquiring Turso
stories.author: cvburgess
bullet_points: Supabase is in the process of acquiring Turso.
This acquisition signals a strategic move by Supabase in the developer tooling space.
The integration likely aims to enhance Supabase's database offerings, particularly around SQLite/edge capabilities.

stories.title: Several vulnerabilities have been discovered in the Linux kernel
stories.author: luispa
bullet_points: Vulnerabilities have been identified within the Linux kernel.
Kernel security flaws represent a significant concern for system stability and security.
This is a critical topic for system administrators and developers relying on Linux.

stories.title: Building Sarrera: Self-Hosted Enterprise AI Inference Gateway with RBAC, Token Quotas & Telemetry
stories.author: marioezquerro
bullet_points: Details the architecture for building a self-hosted, private AI inference gateway.
Integrates key tools like LiteLLM, Caddy, Langfuse, and Open WebUI for functionality.
Focuses on enterprise requirements such as Role-Based Access Control (RBAC) and token quotas.
